jobs.title: Senior Technical Product Manager (Biometric Authentication)
jobs.jd_full:
Veriff is building the foundational trust layer of the internet, empowering people to safely and privately prove they are who they say they are. Our identity verification platform powers onboarding and authentication for some of the world's largest marketplaces, fintechs, and platforms. Biometric Authentication is our second-largest product, and it's how we move customers from one-time identity checks to continuous, lifecycle-long trust.

THE OPPORTUNITY

Biometric Authentication turns every verified user into an ongoing, secure relationship: silent re-verification, step-up authentication, and fraud prevention at the moments that matter. The product runs in production at enterprise scale, with real cost, conversion, and latency consequences for major customers.

As this product has grown into a multi-product area, we're hiring a Senior PM to take primary ownership of Biometric Authentication: driving customer research, competitive roadmap strategy, and pricing, in close partnership with machine learning, engineering, design, sales, and GTM. In this role, you'll be expected to operate autonomously with low management overhead, default to cross-functional collaboration, and are comfortable experimenting and shipping fast. You'll bring enough context and judgement to make commercial trade-offs without waiting for direction. You'll be at your best in ambiguous, fast-moving environments and on distributed, international teams.

This is a role for a PM who treats adoption, conversion, and revenue as their own problem, not one who manages a feature backlog and waits for commercial direction.

You’ll help us protect honest people online by:

  • Own the product end-to-end. Take primary ownership of Biometric Authentication: strategy, roadmap, and execution — across a cross-functional squad of ML, engineering, and design.
  • Own a commercial metric. Pick up a revenue, adoption, or conversion metric, diagnose the gap, and design the customer research and process changes to close it alongside sales and GTM.
  • Make decisions at scale. Reason about trade-offs in cost, conversion, and latency against live enterprise contracts, in real production conditions, on a regular basis.
  • Run a tight customer-feedback loop. Turn enterprise customer feedback into a prioritized, defensible roadmap.
  • Own competitive positioning and pricing. Track the biometric and identity landscape and shape packaging and pricing grounded in real unit economics.
  • Operate with high agency. Get to independent operation within ~60 days and start clearing the highest-impact work early.

You are the right future Veriffian for the job if you have:

  • A technical background and fluent with technical systems: distributed transactional systems, machine learning, operational metrics, COGS, and SDK delivery. (Ability to program is a plus; you won't be building ML models but you should be able to do query, debug and do root cause analysis independently)
  • Experience thriving in a scale-up: high ambiguity, fast pace, and challenging environments.
  • Strong understanding of B2B2C user experience: fluency in the end-user experience inside a business product.
  • ~5+ years of product management experience.
  • Experience in fintech or marketplace products.
  • Background in authentication, security, or identity.
  • Ability to program is a plus; you won't be building ML models but you should be able to do query, debug and do root cause analysis independently)
  • Previous Software Engineering / Data Science development experience

Why Veriff?

We are the preferred identity verification platform partner for the world’s most innovative growth-driven organizations helping conveniently verify and safeguard users anywhere in the world. We support the broadest number of identity documents from nearly every country and territory in the world - and this is continually increasing! With a diverse team in the United States, United Kingdom, Spain, and Estonia, as well as robust backing and funding from investors including Accel, Alkeon, IVP, Tiger Capital, and Y Combinator, we’re dedicated to helping businesses and individuals build a safer and more secure world. We strive to be the benchmark for trust online, and we take pride in being a positive force.When you join Team Veriff, we offer you the opportunity to have a real impact and advance your career whilst looking after you along the way with a range of benefits designed with you in mind. Some of our favourites include...

  • Flexibility to work from home
  • Stock options that ensure your share in our success
  • Extra recharge days on top of your annual vacation
  • Extensive medical, dental, and vision insurance to ensure you’re feeling great physically and mentally
  • Learning and Development & Health and Sports budget that you are free to tailor to your own needs
  • Four weeks of fully paid sabbatical leave after reaching your 5th work anniversary

We are an Equal Opportunities employer committed to a diverse and representative team. Different opinions, perspectives, and personalities push us forward. We want to hear from people who are passionate about their work and align with our values. Regardless of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, or disability. jobs.title: Lead Product Manager

At UpGuard, we are replacing manual security bottlenecks with AI-driven precision. Fresh off a US$75M Series C, we are scaling our infrastructure to process 100 billion risk signals daily. This isn’t just growth; it’s a total reimagining of how the world manages cyber risk.

We build the Cyber Risk Posture Management (CRPM) platform that security teams actually love. By integrating security ratings, threat intel, and agentic AI, we empower organisations to stay ahead of an ever evolving attack surface.

We aren’t just building another tool; we’re defining a category. We provide the autonomy to ship world-class technology and the resources to do it at a global scale.

jobs.title: Sales & Operations Specialist, RC Capital
jobs.jd_full:
RevenueCat gives app businesses the infrastructure and tools to build, run, and improve their monetization. Since graduating from YC's S18 batch, we've grown into the default monetization platform for mobile.

We're in 50%+ of newly shipped subscription apps, we process $16B+ in annual purchase volume, and we help everyone from a solo developer to the OpenAI mobile team understand and grow their revenue.

We're a remote-first team of 150+ people across 25+ countries, guided by values we actually practice: Customer Obsession, Always Be Shipping, Own It, and Balance.

This isn't the right fit for everyone. The systems you’ll build here manage billions of dollars and touch hundreds of millions of end users, and we don’t take that lightly. You'll be expected to work hard and hold a high bar for what you ship, alongside some of the sharpest, most driven people you've worked with. If that sounds energizing rather than exhausting, keep reading.

The Role

RC Capital is RevenueCat's first move into financial services. Our first product, Early Payouts, gives developers access to App Store proceeds without waiting the usual 30 to 60 days for Apple and Google to pay them.

As Sales & Operations Specialist, RC Capital, you will own the customer lifecycle end-to-end - from identifying and qualifying suitable prospects through screening, onboarding, activation, ongoing support, account operations, and portfolio health. You will combine commercial judgment, customer care, operational discipline, and risk awareness to help RC Capital acquire and serve more healthy customers.

This is a hands-on individual-contributor role on a small founding team. You might move from a discovery call to an onboarding issue, a portfolio review, and a workflow improvement in the same day. You will work closely with Sales, Support, Product, Data, Finance, Legal, Marketing, and GTM Operations, and report to the VP of Strategy & Operations. You will also help build the playbook and systems future teammates inherit.

What You'll Own:

  • Sales and qualification. Manage a portfolio of inbound and targeted outbound opportunities. Run discovery, assess product and customer fit, coordinate screening, handle objections, maintain momentum, and guide suitable prospects to a clear decision.

  • Onboarding and activation. Lead approved customers from decision to activated. Ensure customers understand how to use Early Payouts successfully.

  • Customer support and portfolio operations. Serve as a reliable point of contact for customers, including questions, disputes, and operational issues. Coordinate with RevenueCat Support and specialist teams, and own follow-through through resolution.

  • Risk-aware execution. Apply documented customer, fraud, and risk policies consistently; investigate issues; document decisions; monitor emerging patterns; and make sound recommendations. Escalate exceptions and regulated or high-impact decisions to the appropriate risk, legal, finance, or leadership owner.

  • Lifecycle performance and insight. Maintain a reliable view of pipeline, onboarding, support demand, usage, and portfolio health. Turn data into recommendations on funnel quality, conversion, time to activation, drop-off, retention, customer experience, and risk indicators. Bring structured customer insight to Product to inform roadmaps.

  • Systems, automation, and playbooks. Improve CRM, support workflows, internal handoffs, reporting, documentation, and automation. Use AI thoughtfully to reduce manual work and response times without weakening controls or customer trust. Partner with Marketing, Operations, Data, and Product on durable implementations.

  • Customer and growth. Partner with Marketing on focused acquisition and lifecycle experiments. Support marketing efforts like campaign execution, competitive analysis, and content that drives demand.

What We're Looking For

  • 4+ years in a high-ownership, customer-facing commercial or operations role spanning sales, account management, customer success, customer support, or customer operations.

  • A track record of moving opportunities through a commercial process and managing a meaningful volume of customer relationships with strong follow-through.

  • Experience in fintech, payments, lending, factoring, embedded finance, or another environment where customer growth and operational risk are closely connected.

  • 1-2 years of marketing or growth experience running campaigns or managing CRM-driven outreach.

  • Strong operational judgment: you clarify ownership, define next steps, document decisions, apply policy consistently, and recognize when an issue needs specialist review.

  • Analytical fluency across CRM, support, and analytics tools, with the ability to diagnose funnel or portfolio performance and recommend action.

  • Practical experience improving workflows with automation and AI, including judgment about where automation introduces unacceptable risk or a poor customer experience.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication: persuasive with prospects, clear during onboarding, calm in disputes, and concise with executives and cross-functional partners.

  • Comfort operating in ambiguity on a small, autonomous team and working hours that meaningfully overlap with US time zones.

Nice to Have

  • Direct experience with payment operations, underwriting, fraud and risk workflows, disputes, or compliance-adjacent processes.

  • Experience launching a new product, business line, or operating motion before the playbook was written.

  • Knowledge of mobile apps, developer products, subscriptions, or App Store economics.

  • Experience contributing to CRM or lifecycle campaigns, customer-facing content, or growth experiments.

  • Familiarity with tools such as Salesforce, Notion, Linear, Intercom or Zendesk, Slack, Zoom, and product analytics platforms.

What success looks like

In your first 30 days

  • Understand RC Capital's product, customers, unit economics, risk model, and role within RevenueCat.

  • Map the lifecycle from first signal through activation and live-account support.

  • Establish baseline reporting for pipeline quality, conversion, time to decision, time to activation, support demand, repeat usage, and portfolio health.

  • Shadow sales, onboarding, support, risk, and account reviews; then handle initial customer interactions with support.

  • Ship one concrete improvement to a workflow, report, playbook, or automation.

By 90 days

  • Independently own a portfolio from qualification and screening through onboarding and ongoing operations, escalating genuine exceptions appropriately.

  • Give the team a reliable view of pipeline, onboarding, support, usage, and portfolio performance, with recommendations rather than reporting alone.

  • Run a consistent cadence for opportunity follow-up, onboarding, live-account reviews, and issue resolution.

  • Ship workflow or automation improvements that reduce manual work or customer wait time without weakening controls.

  • Support marketing efforts to deliver on targets.

  • Translate recurring customer and operational friction into structured recommendations for Product, Data, Finance, Legal, Support, or Marketing.

By 6 to 12 months

  • Improve key lifecycle measures such as conversion, activation speed, utilization and retention.

  • Help grow a portfolio of healthy customers while keeping fraud, disputes, losses, and other agreed risk indicators within guardrails.

  • Maintain a commercial and customer-operations playbook another teammate can follow without relying on context held only in people's heads.

  • Help turn the early motion into a repeatable engine and identify which responsibilities should move to partner teams or future hires as volume grows.

What we offer:

  • Competitive equity in a fast-growing, Series C startup backed by top-tier investors, including Y Combinator

  • 10-year window to exercise vested equity options

  • A fully remote environment designed around autonomy and flexibility

  • 4-5 weeks of flexible time off annually

  • Paid desk at a co-working space

  • Workspace budget and continuous learning stipend

Interviewing at RevenueCat

Our interview process is rigorous on purpose. We want to be sure that everyone we bring on is genuinely excited about this work, aligned with how we operate, and ready to meet our high bar for performance. Curious what that actually looks like? Read more in our blog post on how we hire at RevenueCat, including tips to help you succeed.

Senior Product Manager

Handbooks, Compliance Learning, and Multi-State Compliance

Workforce Compliance  |  Reports to: Senior Director, Product Management  |  Mitratech US

At Mitratech, we are a team of innovators focused on building world-class products that simplify operations in the Legal, Risk, Compliance, and HR functions. We are a close-knit, globally dispersed team that thrives in an ecosystem that supports individual excellence and takes pride in its diverse and inclusive work culture centered around great people practices, learning opportunities, and having fun! Our culture is the ideal blend of entrepreneurial spirit and enterprise investment, enabling the chance to move at a rapid pace with some of the most complex, leading-edge technologies available.

For over 35 years, the experts at Mitratech have been focused on solving the complex needs. Today, we serve 20,000 client companies of all sizes globally, representing 30% of the Fortune 500 and over 500,000 users in over 160 countries.

As we continue to grow, we’re always looking for resourceful, enthusiastic, and fresh perspectives. Join our global team and see what makes Mitratech a truly exceptional place to work!

About the Team

Mitratech Workforce Compliance turns constantly changing labor and employment law into a strategic advantage for US employers of every size. Our ARIES Intelligence Core combines an expert-curated labor law corpus, agentic AI, and certified HR experts to assure compliance everywhere employment law introduces risk: every law, every policy, every employee, from sourcing to termination. We reach employers directly and through partners, including brokers, carriers, PEOs, and HCM and payroll platforms.

This role sits on our newly formed Workforce Compliance product team. The team exists to own the customer problem end to end: understanding the buyer, the user, the approver, and the accountable owner behind every compliance job, and shaping one coherent product direction across the portfolio. We build once on shared intelligence and reusable capabilities, we lean on licensed experts for judgment, and we hold ourselves to evidence over opinion. Product managers here decide within their scope, raise concerns while they are still small, and communicate clearly so that decisions get made faster.

Job Overview

Mitratech is seeking a Senior Product Manager to own the customer problem of keeping a growing, multi-location workforce compliant with the policies, notices, and training the law requires. Your primary products are Handbooks and compliance learning. Your workflow scope covers Multi-State and Jurisdiction Management and Onboarding, excluding I-9 and E-Verify, which is owned by peera.

Multi-state compliance and handbook confusion is the single largest theme in our customer and prospect conversations today. Employers who built a business in one state and expanded to three do not know what changed, usually find out after a mistake, and are maintaining a handbook by copy and paste. Brokers and PEOs who deliver that handbook under their own brand cannot always prove it is current or that it is being used. Employees rarely see or acknowledge the policies that protect both sides. Producing a compliant handbook today is time consuming and often requires rounds of revision. We believe that the process should be efficient and that delivering insights to the right system or person at the right time should be paramount.

You will own that problem across every channel we sell through: our own product, partner platforms, chat, and authorized agents calling our Intelligence Core. You will decide which customer journeys come first, what the shared handbook engine must do, how policy changes flow into acknowledgments, training assignments, and downstream HR and payroll settings, and how we prove the outcome to the employer and to the partner who sponsored it.

What you will own

  • Handbooks: intake, policy selection and assembly from verified content, multi-state and section-level editing, review and human approval, versioning, publication, and portability of the employer’s handbook across sponsor and broker changes
  • Learn and Compliance Learning: mandated training (harassment prevention, safety, and similar) assigned and tracked against the jurisdictions where employees actually work, and the proof of completion that goes with it
  • Multi-State and Jurisdiction Management: the employer’s jurisdiction footprint as a shared, reusable input that triggers the right policies, notices, training, and alerts when a workforce crosses a state line or a headcount threshold
  • Onboarding (excluding I-9 and E-Verify): new-hire state reporting, wage theft prevention notices, and handbook and policy acknowledgment at hire and at every policy update
  • The post-approval loop: distribution to employees, acknowledgment tracking, manager guidance, and a human-reviewed handoff of policy changes to payroll and HRIS configuration
  • How these experiences show up inside partner platforms and through the Intelligence Core API, with attribution that travels with our content

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Own the customer problem

  • Be the person in the company who knows the most about how a multi-location employer, an HR generalist, a broker account manager, and a PEO team actually keep policies and training current today, and where that work breaks
  • Maintain a living view of buyer, user, approver, and accountable owner for each job in your scope, across direct and partner channels
  • Set the outcomes we are aiming for (for example, time to a publishable handbook, share of employees acknowledged, training completion against mandate deadlines) and hold the team to them

Lead customer discovery

  • Run a continuous discovery cadence: weekly conversations with employers, HR practitioners, brokers, PEOs, and our own HR experts, plus regular review of sales and support call evidence
  • Turn what you learn into explicit, testable assumptions. Label what we know, what we assume, and what the evidence supports
  • Collaborate with Product Design to validate solutions with prototypes and small experiments before committing engineering capacity, and be willing to kill ideas the evidence does not support
  • Partner with the persona and research work already underway so the team shares one picture of the customer instead of several

Shape AI-native experiences with experts in the loop

  • Design handbook and training experiences with our Foundations counterparts that gather employer context once, apply cited guidance and expert review, coordinate the approved facts into the document, the acknowledgment, and the training assignment, and prove completion
  • Define where an agent can act, where a human must approve, and where a question routes to a licensed expert.
  • Work with the Intelligence Core team so your experiences draw on the shared labor law corpus and employer context rather than duplicating intelligence

Deliver and measure

  • Write product requirement documents and decision documents that engineering, design, and content experts can act on. Prioritize the backlog and own launch and adoption
  • Define the metrics that show whether the customer problem is actually getting solved, instrument them, and report on them plainly
  • Protect current customer and partner commitments while shaping the next plan, and surface conflicts early

Work across the company

  • Partner with engineering, design, data science, the compliance content team, HR advisory experts, customer success, partner management, and go-to-market
  • Give partners a clear story for how Handbooks and Learn add value in their channel and how they can prove utilization to their own clients
  • Enable sales, support, and implementation on what you ship and why it matters to the employer

What Success Looks Like in Your First Year

  • You have interviewed dozens of employers, practitioners, and partners and produced a synthesis the whole team uses to prioritize
  • The handbook production cycle is measurably shorter and the causes of revision churn are understood and shrinking
  • Multi-state, section-level handbook editing is in customers’ hands and partners can point to acknowledgment and training evidence at renewal
  • A validated, human-reviewed handoff from approved policy changes to employee distribution and payroll configuration exists, with clear ownership
  • Your scope has explicit success measures, a sequenced plan, and documented decisions on what changed and what stayed in place

How We Work

We are a new team with a clear direction and a lot still to shape. The product leaders who do well here share a few habits:

  • Precision about the problem. You know the customer, the job, and the evidence before you become attached to a solution, and you can separate what we know from what we assume.
  • Judgment, not permission-seeking. You know when to decide, when to run a test, and when a tradeoff needs a wider conversation.
  • Clear written thinking. You produce short, decision-ready documents rather than long decks.
  • Direct feedback, in both directions. You give it constructively and you ask for it.
  • Early and messy beats late and polished. A heads-up on a risk is always welcome.

Requirements & Skills

  • 5+ years of product management experience in B2B SaaS, with at least 3 years owning a product area end to end, from problem definition through launch, adoption, and iteration
  • A demonstrated practice of continuous customer discovery: you talk to customers and users every week, you can show the interview notes and synthesis behind your last three roadmap decisions, and you can explain which assumptions you tested and which you got wrong
  • Experience serving two or more distinct audiences for the same product (for example, a partner who buys and an employer who uses) and designing for the tension between them
  • Track record of writing product requirements and decision documents that engineering, design, and compliance experts could act on without a follow-up meeting
  • Comfort defining and defending success metrics, then changing course when the data says to
  • Experience working alongside subject-matter experts (legal, compliance, clinical, or similar) where the product has to be right, not just shipped
  • Strong collaboration with engineering, design, and data science in agile environments, including shaping AI-assisted or agentic experiences with clear human review points

We are seeking an AI SaaS Product Manager to own the released application portfolio built in-house by the AI & Autonomy division — the AI-powered web, mobile, and spatial applications used daily by manufacturing, satellite operations, analytics, and executive teams, along with AI capabilities delivered to telecom partners. This person is the connective tissue between the engineers who build these applications, the internal customers who depend on them, and the IT organization that helps support them, deciding what ships next based on real usage and ensuring everything that ships is documented, learnable, and supportable. As the organization matures its operational support model for AI applications, this role also supports the Chief of AI and Autonomy in executing the transition roadmap that moves these applications from build-team support into steady-state operations. This is a hands-on, writing-heavy product role for someone fluent enough in AI/ML systems to document them accurately, and user-obsessed enough to measure success by adoption, time-to-resolution, and how rarely people need to ask for help.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Own the post-launch product lifecycle for the AI division’s released applications — prioritizing enhancements, defects, and retirements based on usage data, user feedback, and business impact — and maintain a published roadmap internal customers can plan against.
  • Partner daily with the full-stack, ML, and data science engineering teams to translate user needs into clear requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria; participate in sprint planning, backlog grooming, and release readiness reviews.
  • Run structured discovery with internal customers — quality inspectors, manufacturing engineers, satellite operations staff, analysts, and executives — through interviews, floor-side shadowing, and usage analytics, converting what you learn into prioritized product decisions.
  • Define and track product success metrics for each released application (adoption, active usage, task completion, feature engagement, support volume, user satisfaction) and report them to the Chief of AI and Autonomy.
  • Own release readiness as a gate: no application ships without release notes, updated user documentation, a known-issues list, and an agreed support plan.
  • Write and maintain end-user product documentation for every released application — getting-started guides, workflow walkthroughs, feature references, administrator guides, and versioned release notes.
  • Design and maintain in-app guidance: onboarding tours, contextual help, empty states, and error messaging written so users can self-correct without filing a ticket.
  • Build and maintain the self-help troubleshooting library — a catalog of common errors, their causes, and step-by-step resolution paths mapped to actual error codes and failure modes, including AI-specific ones such as low-confidence predictions, model timeouts, and degraded offline sync.
  • Partner with engineering to ensure errors are instrumented, human-readable, and traceable, turning raw exceptions and API failures into diagnosable user-facing messages with documented remediation steps.
  • Co-own the support model with Corporate IT: define tiering and escalation paths, write the IT-facing runbooks and triage scripts used at first contact, and train the help desk on each application before it launches.
  • Serve as the escalation point for internal customer issues IT cannot resolve — coordinating with engineering on root cause, workarounds, and permanent fixes, and closing the loop with the affected users.
  • Support the Chief of AI and Autonomy in building and executing the transition roadmap as the organization matures its operational support model for AI applications — tracking phases, milestones, and readiness criteria, and flagging risks to the handoff of operational ownership from engineering to steady-state operations.
  • Partner with factory NOC staff to define how each released AI application is monitored and supported in production: service catalog entries, health dashboards, alert thresholds and routing, on-call rotations, and escalation paths.
  • Help coordinate across the internal AI research lab, data center operations, engineering, and Corporate IT to document clear ownership (RACI) for applications, models, and the compute and network infrastructure they run on, so nothing falls between teams during the transition.
  • Write NOC-facing runbooks, standard operating procedures, and incident playbooks for every application; prepare and facilitate transition readiness reviews and tabletop exercises before each responsibility moves.
  • Help put incident, problem, and change management practices in place with the NOC — post-incident reviews, change calendars, and planned-maintenance communications to internal customers — so users experience the transition as continuity, not disruption.
  • Analyze support tickets and self-help usage to identify recurring failure patterns, feeding documentation updates, UX fixes, and backlog items that measurably reduce ticket volume over time.
  • Establish and report service metrics for the portfolio: first-contact resolution, time-to-resolution, self-service deflection, documentation coverage, and user satisfaction.
  • Own the documentation system itself — information architecture, style guide, templates, review cadence, and version control — so content stays accurate as applications evolve release over release.
  • Run enablement for every new release: launch communications, training sessions, office hours, and champion networks inside each internal customer organization.
  • Support partner-facing AI features with externally appropriate documentation, onboarding material, and support workflows in coordination with the teams serving telecom partners.

Qualifications

Education:

Bachelor’s degree in a technical, business, or communications field, or equivalent experience.

Experience:

  • Simplify unnecessary handoffs, manual steps, exceptions and operational complexity.

Our vibrant offices in Amsterdam and Lisbon are designed to inspire collaboration. Most Catawikians operate in a hybrid setup, combining office-based and remote work, with a minimum of two days per week in the office, unless a role is explicitly stated as fully remote or fully office-based.
